newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close at session highs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close at session highs.

text.p: Argentine stocks resumed their upward bounce and closed at session highs Monday, boosted by powerful rallies on Wall Street and the main European markets, dealers said.
"The bolsa tracked the international markets higher today, but there is a prevailing sense of caution which kept liquidity tight and buying selective," said Gabriel Ruiz of brokers Tavelli.
The blue-chip MerVal index, which advanced 1.8 percent last week, rose 1.6 percent to close at 742. The broad market tacked on 1.8 percent.
Floor volume fell to 23.9 million pesos from 29.3 million Friday, while over-the-counter volume shrank to 108.5 million pesos from 154 million Friday.

"The market rose but people weren't very enthusiastic today," another trader said. "Nobody really believes yet that we've resumed the upward course we halted two weeks ago, and these doubts will probably linger until we have fresh inflation data in the United States shedding light on the future direction of interest rates."
Session risers beat decliners 43 to 10 and 14 issues closed flat.

Top MerVal risers were steelmakers Siderca and Acindar, up 4.3 percent and 3.6 percent respectively, and Banco Frances, up 3.6 percent. Losers were led by construction stock Polledo, off 1.8 percent, and oil company Astra, down 0.6 percent.

Traders noted foods giant Molinos switched to losses late in the day after the company announced a fourth-quarter loss of $0.8 million, compared to average earnings of $7.2 million in each of the previous three quarters for a yearly profit of $20.7 million. The stock closed off 0.5 percent at $3.78.
